solutions.check: 28 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), as the answer another puzzle gave the same clue, or as the one past answer its crossings left that the printed letters allow, agrees with the 27 answers the paper printed; printed-crossing fills: 4-down

clue.text: Face up to Conservative in foremost position

parts.note: the front is the position at the very fore

explanation.surface: A Tory politician confronts a challenge from the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here: the abbreviation simply comes before the word for the leading position.
explanation.definitionFit: To confront something is to meet it head-on and deal with it.

parts.note: 'singular' suggests odd, but here means made as a single item, such as a swimsuit

explanation.surface: An eccentric outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece is a garment, typically a swimsuit, made in a single part.

clue.text: Do what Jack did for couturier's

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme 'This is the house that Jack built', so to do the same is to construct a dwelling
a designer's business producing high-fashion clothes

explanation.surface: Copying a nursery rhyme hero for a dress designer.
explanation.definitionFit: To fashion a house is to build one, as Jack did; a fashion house is a couturier's firm.

definitions.meaning: to talk candidly, holding nothing back
guns open up when they begin firing

explanation.surface: A gunman talked openly and then began firing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone confiding has stopped holding back; guns that begin firing are said to do the same.

clue.text: Finished most of the longest part, of course

indicators.note: most of the word means dropping its last letter

parts.note: on a golf course the rough is the long grass bordering the fairways

explanation.surface: Having completed the greater part of a long course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a golf course, where the rough is the longest grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Being through with something means having finished it.

clue.text: This novel abridged for Betjeman's mountainous sports girl

definitions.meaning: Samuel Richardson's 1740 epistolary novel about a virtuous servant girl

definitions.text: abridged for Betjeman's mountainous sports girl
definitions.meaning: John Betjeman's poem 'Pot Pourri from a Surrey Garden' hails 'Pam, I adore you, Pam, you great big mountainous sports girl'; Pam is the shortened name

explanation.surface: A classic novel cut down to fit a poet's athletic heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Richardson's novel bears this title, and its short form is the name of Betjeman's hearty sporting girl.

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
to lam is to beat or strike

explanation.surface: A single strike brought down a republic's government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns ILAM backwards; the result is a West African republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked republic in West Africa.

clue.text: One of those taking risks, possibly turn and turn about

indicators.note: the second word for turning goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: to veer is to turn or change direction

indicators.note: possibly says the first 'turn' may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A risk-taker might take turns in alternation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the first TURN into NTUR, and 'about' puts VEER (the second 'turn') around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A venturer is someone who ventures, an adventurer who takes chances.

clue.text: Source of Mill's power to lead people

parts.note: to head a group is to lead it
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Something powering John Stuart Mill's ability to lead others.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital M makes 'Mill' look like the philosopher, but it is a watermill; the apostrophe hides the lowercase sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A headrace is the channel bringing water to a mill wheel, supplying its power.

clue.text: Piles of sand no longer in river

definitions.meaning: golfers once teed up on small heaps of sand before wooden or plastic pegs replaced them

explanation.surface: Sandbanks that have disappeared from a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf tees were formerly little sand heaps, and the Tees is a river flowing past Middlesbrough.

parts.note: to hand over something is to surrender it
'dukes' is slang for fists, so a duke is a fist

explanation.surface: A duke gives up his position without a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke' looks like a nobleman but is slang for a fist ('put up your dukes').
explanation.definitionFit: Making money hand over fist means gaining it rapidly and with little effort.

indicators.note: the enclosure word goes inside the abbey's name

parts.note: Fountains Abbey is a famous ruined Cistercian abbey in Yorkshire
to pen an animal is to shut it up in an enclosure

explanation.surface: Authors confined in a monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: Fountains Abbey is a ruined monastery in North Yorkshire; PEN goes before its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Fountain pens are instruments for writing, so they are writers.

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so these six letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Something accomplished through a revolution in history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' rearranges DONE and BY into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond and past both mean further than, as in going past or beyond a limit.

indicators.note: 'sort of' says these letters are only loosely the words given, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tough, determined old country horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gritty' looks like a description of the nag's character, but it means grainy; 'sort of' rearranges RURAL NAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gritty is made of small grains or particles, like sand.

clue.text: Hope rhapsody can reveal this? Possibly

indicators.note: the words can reveal a run of letters lying across their boundary

explanation.surface: A rhapsody might express hope, or it might not.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the end of 'Hope' into 'rhapsody'; 'this' points the solver to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps and possibly both express that something may or may not be so.

indicators.note: the word for information is placed inside the word for factory

parts.note: a plant is an industrial factory
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Booming news coming from a works.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British informal slang for information or facts.
explanation.definitionFit: A plangent sound is loud and reverberating, often mournfully so.

parts.note: to fiddle about is to potter, keeping idly busy

explanation.surface: A deputy watches from the sidelines, playing second fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second fiddle' reads as a phrase for an underling but splits into S and a word for tinkering about.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotter watches out for things, such as aircraft or trains.

clue.text: Energetically begin to note movement of vessel

parts.note: to pitch in is to set to work with vigour
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: Getting stuck in to record how a ship moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' is a musical note, G, not a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's pitching is its up-and-down plunging motion, fore and aft.

clue.text: Work out task given in school

definitions.meaning: to train the body, or to use a power
a piece of set work for pupils

explanation.definitionFit: To exercise is to work out physically, and an exercise is a set piece of practice work in class.

clue.text: Beauty less dangerous than femme fatale?

definitions.meaning: a fatal woman kills, whereas one who merely stuns leaves her victim alive

explanation.surface: A lovely woman who is not quite deadly.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunner is a gorgeous person, and literally one who knocks you out rather than kills.

indicators.note: the adhesive is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a rent is a tear or opening
gum is glue, something that makes things stick

explanation.surface: Someone joins a quarrel by poking a stick into a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is the quarrel sense, rhyming with 'cow', not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A row is a noisy quarrel, a heated dispute.

definitions.meaning: in King Lear the Earl of Gloucester's illegitimate son schemes against his brother Edgar
the East Anglian king martyred by the Danes in 869 and venerated at Bury St ...

explanation.surface: The Earl of Gloucester's son is a holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's villainous bastard son in King Lear and the martyred king of East Anglia share this name.

clue.text: Split between 10 in stand that's right

indicators.note: the word for split sits between the two letters

parts.note: 10-across is TEES, read as Ts, two letter T's
to rive is to split or tear apart

explanation.surface: A stand divided among the answers in a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10-across answer is read as the plural of the letter T, giving two T's around RIVE. 'Right as a trivet' is an old saying for perfectly well, so a trivet is the stand that's right.
explanation.definitionFit: A trivet is a three-legged stand for a pot, proverbially steady in 'right as a trivet'.

parts.note: 16-across read as S. Potter, the author Stephen Potter, whose book described the art of winning games by dubious tricks

explanation.surface: How a sharp-eyed observer manages to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 16-across splits as S POTTER, i.e. Stephen Potter, the British humorist who wrote a famous 1947 book on winning without actually cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Potter's book of that title describes ploys for winning games by unsettling opponents.

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the 7-down answer is to be rearranged

parts.note: 7-down is the republic MALI

explanation.surface: Correspondence coming from a numbered clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the four letters of the answer to 7-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail is the post, the letters and parcels delivered.

definitions.meaning: in Anglo-Saxon and Irish law a killer paid compensation to the victim's kin; the Irish term is this word
Dean Farrar's Victorian school story '..., or Little by Little' is a famous moralising tale

explanation.surface: A killer pays his penalty in a story with a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: The eric was an old Irish blood-fine for homicide, and Farrar's 'Eric' is a byword for a preachy Victorian moral story.

indicators.note: the small word breaks into the word for gradation

parts.note: a nuance is a fine gradation or shade of difference

explanation.surface: A tedious speaker breaks into a degree ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'graduation' looks like a degree ceremony but means a gradual shading, a nuance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bore and a nuisance are both people or things that are tiresome to have around.

definitions.meaning: to write down officially, as in a list
to display a reading, as a meter does

explanation.definitionFit: To register is to put on record, and also to show, as a dial registers a temperature.
